Cusco · Perú

Church of the Nativity, Chinchero

A painted church on an Inca foundation

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

The church occupies the upper plaza in Chinchero’s monumental ensemble. Originally dedicated to Nuestra Señora de Monserrat, it is now known as the Church of the Nativity. The shift from Inca masonry below to a painted Christian worship space is central to the visit.

Planning your visit

30–45 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

A painted church on an Inca foundation

Use the upper plaza to show the church against its Inca stone base. Interior photography depends on parish instructions; a view of the threshold often tells the architectural story clearly.

History and local experience

Read the shift in building materials at the plaza edge before stepping inside. The external stone base and the religious paintings belong to related but distinct episodes in Chinchero’s history.

Walking route

  1. Plaza de Chinchero, Templo de Nuestra Señora de la Natividad
  2. Cross the upper plaza to see the church front, ask the parish about entry and follow the open aisle if visiting is permitted.
  3. The park ticket and church access should be checked separately.
